limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not determine whether dense collagen regions precede tumor formation, result from tumor contraction, or arise from fibroblast activation.
The causal relationship between collagen alignment and invasion is suggested but not directly tested in vivo; evidence is correlational from imaging and supported by explant experiments.
Quantitative sample sizes (n) and statistical tests for TACS observations are not reported.
Imaging depth is limited to 440 nm, which may not capture full tissue thickness.
The study uses mouse models (Wnt-1, PyVT, col1a1) and may not fully recapitulate human tumor-stromal interactions.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

experiments_or_tasks: Histology, electron microscopy, and nonlinear optical imaging of epithelial-stromal interactions in normal mammary glands, mammary tumors, and tumor explants in 3D culture.
Multiphoton laser-scanning microscopy (MPLSM) and second harmonic generation (SHG) imaging of intact, unfixed, unsectioned mammary glands from normal, col1a1 transgenic, Wnt-1, and PyVT mice.

methods.name: Multiphoton laser-scanning microscopy (MPLSM) with second harmonic generation (SHG)
methods.protocol_description: MPLSM was used to generate multiphoton excitation of endogenous fluorophores and SHG to image stromal collagen in live, intact, unfixed, unsectioned mammary glands. Imaging was performed ex vivo on tumor tissue. Collagen density was quantified by area of collagen signal and signal intensity.
